stem.en: The experiment is repeated with a gold foil ten times thicker, but the particles are still able to get through it. What change do you expect in the results?

text.en: More particles are turned aside or bounced back, because each particle now passes close to more nuclei.
The results do not change, because the atoms of gold are the same in both foils.
No particle gets through, because a thick foil has no empty space left in it.

explanation.en: The atoms are the same, but a thicker foil has more layers of atoms, so each particle has more chances of coming close to a nucleus. Those atoms are still mostly empty space, however many layers there are, so many particles still get through.

hints.en: Thin or thick, what decides whether a particle turns? Count how many nuclei it could meet on the way.
